name: Maine
summary: Statutes: legislature.maine.gov serves one static HTML page per section at a URL built straight from the citation (title + section, letters and hyphens kept), plus per-section, per-chapter and per-title PDF/Word files; the text is expressly unofficial (the certified text is the M.R.S.A.), and Justia 2025 is the tier-2 fallback. Session laws: the Law and Legislative Digital Library serves one PDF per chapter at a constructible URL. Constitution: the Revisor's full-text PDF and HTML (through CR 2023, cc. 1-2). Court rules: full-set PDFs on courts.maine.gov (civil 640K chars, criminal 275K) need the script or corpus. Case law: Law Court opinions 2017-present as PDFs keyed by the public-domain cite (2024 ME 84 → 24me084.pdf); 1997-2016 only on Justia; Maine Reports 1-161 (1820-1965, official pagination) as scanned volumes on lldc. The Code of Maine Rules and weekly rulemaking notices on www.maine.gov are bot-walled; Cornell LII's CMR is the only readable admin-code route.

citation_map.notes: Maine style (M.R. App. P. and the Law Court's opinions) cites statutes as '14 M.R.S. § 752 (2024)' (M.R.S. replaced M.R.S.A. in 2009; the year names the M.R.S.A. volume/pamphlet). Bluebook: 'Me. Rev. Stat. Ann. tit. 14, § 752' (21st ed. 'Me. Stat. tit. 14, § 752'). Statute titles carry letter suffixes (17-A, 18-C, 39-A) and sections carry letter suffixes (752-C, 4572-A, 1711-C) or UCC-style hyphenation in a few titles (11 M.R.S. § 2-314, § 1-1201; 18-C § 1-201): the URL keeps them verbatim. A '§§ 751-753' range is a span, not a hyphenated section: the regex refuses it and captures only the first section. Session laws: Maine cites 'P.L. 2023, ch. 405' with the first year of the Legislature (chapters of the second regular session continue the same series and keep that year: P.L. 2023, c. 679 was enacted in 2024); private and special laws 'P. & S.L.', resolves 'Resolve 2023, ch. 86', constitutional resolutions 'CR 2023, c. 1'. Bare 'P.L. YYYY, c. N' is also New Jersey's and Pennsylvania's form, so it routes here only with Maine context. Constitution: Article IV is in Parts (pt. 1-3; Maine text says 'Part First'); Article I is the Declaration of Rights (bare 'Declaration of Rights' is also MA, MD, NH: do not route on it). Court rules: Maine abbreviates 'M.R. Civ. P.', 'M.R. Evid.', 'M.R. App. P.', 'M.R.U. Crim. P.' (unified rules, since 2015; the older 'M.R. Crim. P.' applied before), 'M.R. Prof. Conduct'; Montana uses 'M. R. Civ. P.' / 'M. R. Evid.' / 'M. R. App. P.' so the bare M.R. forms are context_required and the 'Me. R.' and prose forms are distinctive. Montana's own M. R. patterns (data/mt.json) are not context_required and will claim Maine's M.R. examples: that is a conflict to fix in the Montana record. Case law: public-domain citation 'YYYY ME N' (since 1997), pinpoint '¶ N'; reported opinions also in A.2d/A.3d, which the court calls the permanent official version (since 1966). Maine Reports (Me.) ran to vol. 161 (1965). Memoranda of decision are cited 'Mem 26-139' (Mem-YY-N) and are not precedential (M.R. App. P. 12(c)). Law Court dockets are county-coded: 'And-23-68' (Androscoggin), 'Cum-17-54'; BCD = Business and Consumer Docket, WCB = Workers' Compensation Board appeals. Trial-court decisions are cited by WL/LEXIS ('2019 WL ... (Me. Super. Ct. ...)', 'Me. Super. LEXIS', 'Me. Bus. & Consumer LEXIS') plus docket (e.g. 'CV-2019-123', 'BCD-CV-2019-45'); a WL number cannot be resolved to a free URL. CourtListener ids are from memory and unverified.

sources.title: Maine Revised Statutes (Office of the Revisor of Statutes)
sources.publisher: Maine Legislature, Office of the Revisor of Statutes
sources.official_status_evidence: Per-section PDF footer (e.g. https://legislature.maine.gov/statutes/14/title14sec752.pdf): a version 'not been officially certified by the Secretary of State'; refer to the Maine Revised Statutes Annotated for certified text. The State claims copyright in its codified statutes and asks republishers to carry a disclaimer.
sources.coverage: All titles of the Maine Revised Statutes (Titles 1-39-A incl. lettered titles 7-A … 39-A); one HTML page per section, plus PDF and Word per section, chapter and title.

access.pattern_rules: title verbatim incl. letter suffix in upper case (14, 17-A, 39-A); section verbatim incl. hyphen and letter suffix in upper case (752, 752-C, 2-314 for 11 M.R.S. § 2-314, 4572-A). Subsections are on the section page (no anchors needed). A non-existent section returns HTTP 404 (title14sec9999.html), never a soft page. Same stem with .pdf or .docx gives the section PDF / Word file. Chapter page: /statutes/{title}/title{title}ch{chapter}sec0.html (section links, no text); chapter PDF /statutes/{title}/title{title}ch{chapter}.pdf; title TOC /statutes/{title}/title{title}ch0sec0.html; whole title /statutes/{title}/title{title}.pdf (and .docx).
access.navigation: Not needed for a cited section. For browsing: list of titles → title TOC (title{T}ch0sec0.html), which DOES show section ranges per chapter ('Chapter 205: LIMITATION OF ACTIONS §751 - §871') → chapter page (section links only) → section page.

automation.notes: WebFetch reads a section page in full when the URL was reached from a fetched page (statutes index → title TOC → chapter page → section). A section URL typed from the pattern hit a permission prompt that timed out (gated) on 2026-10-17; use fetch_doc.py for built URLs. Section pages are small (2-13K chars); no truncation.
